evals.prompt: I have buzz-cli built and BUZZ_RELAY_URL already points at our staging relay. Create a private channel called release-ops, add the agent pubkey from $AGENT_PUBKEY, post RELEASE READY from release-note.md without shell expansion, and verify the message can be read back. Do not expose either private key.
evals.expected_output: Uses current buzz help to verify syntax, confirms the staging target before writes, uses the CLI and stdin for content, captures channel/event IDs, adds membership, reads the message back, and never prints secrets.

evals.prompt: In my local block/buzz checkout, add a new agent-facing action that archives a project note. Work out which crates/files should change, implement it, and run the narrowest meaningful tests before the full gate.
evals.expected_output: Reads local AGENTS.md, relevant vision/component docs and live CLI structure; prefers a Nostr event where appropriate; routes agent-facing behavior through buzz-cli; keeps tenant/auth boundaries; adds tests and runs focused checks before just ci.

evals.prompt: Upgrade our self-hosted Buzz Docker Compose deployment on a VPS. We use Caddy TLS and want minimal downtime. Tell me exactly what to inspect, back up, run, and verify. The checkout may be several weeks behind upstream.
evals.expected_output: Inspects the deployed revision and upstream current docs, requires backups of secrets/identity/Postgres/object/git/Caddy state, validates config, pins an artifact, uses the supported run.sh TLS flow, checks probes plus signed functionality, and links exact official Compose/release docs rather than guessing stale flags.

evals.prompt: Our buzz-acp agent has been running for a day and has never answered anyone. The service is active, the logs show no errors, it reports discovering our channels, and it appears in the member list. Where do you look?
evals.expected_output: Recognises this as a delivery-gate result rather than a crash, and works the gates in order: channel membership, subscription (with --subscribe config, a membership without a matching rule is never subscribed), mention filter, then the author gate. Identifies --respond-to owner-only as the default and BUZZ_ACP_AGENT_OWNER being unset or holding the wrong pubkey as the likeliest cause, and checks the resolved value in the startup banner rather than the env file. Recommends allowlist over anyone where the author set is known. Does not start by reading relay logs or restarting the service.

evals.prompt: Our agent answers every message three or four times, and nobody can @-mention it from Buzz Desktop — it doesn't show up in the autocomplete, and in the member list it's just a string of hex. Fix both.
evals.expected_output: Attributes the repetition to --multiple-event-handling defaulting to steer with an adapter that cannot steer, so each mid-turn event becomes cancel+re-prompt, and sets queue. Attributes the missing autocomplete entry to channel role bot being routed through the desktop's managed-agent list (upstream block/buzz#4489) and re-adds the identity as member, noting there is no set-role so it must leave and be re-added. Attributes the hex display to a missing kind:0 profile and runs users set-profile signed by that agent's own key, not an admin's.

evals.prompt: I want an agent in a #bot-factory channel that can provision new agents when I approve. Design it.
evals.expected_output: Treats the approval gate as the core of the design, not an afterthought. Defines the approver structurally — any pubkey that is not one of the provisioned agent identities — rather than hard-coding a single owner pubkey. Normalises approval text before matching (markdown punctuation, whitespace, case), uses a confusable-free ID alphabet, accepts a bare approve resolved to the newest open proposal, scans enough history to catch threaded replies, and offers cancel. Provisions with a distinct keypair, a kind:0 profile, channel role member, and a supervised unit. Keeps the factory's signing key in a root-owned file rather than a secret store the agents themselves can read, and notes that otherwise an agent could approve its own creation.

evals.prompt: Buzz Desktop's Share connection flow against our closed self-hosted relay fails with `WebSocket connection failed: HTTP error: 404 Not Found`. Normal relay messaging works. Diagnose and fix the deployment.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the NIP-43 legacy `/pair` fallback, confirms the 404 with NIP-11 and an upgrade request, deploys the stateless `buzz-pair-relay` sidecar behind TLS, configures `BUZZ_PAIRING_RELAY_URL`, and verifies a 101 WebSocket upgrade plus unaffected signed main-relay access. Uses Compose `entrypoint`, not `command`, for the sidecar and keeps its raw port private.

evals.prompt: My self-hosted Buzz relay advertises push support and logs that the NIP-PL worker started, but my iPhone gets no notifications when the Buzz app is closed. Is my APNs setup broken?
evals.expected_output: Checks current official implementation status before changing permissions or APNs config. Explains that server-side NIP-PL/gateway infrastructure is not end-to-end client support, cites the README and push-gateway relay-integration status, notes the missing current mobile enrollment/lease path and APNs entitlement, checks `push_leases`, and concludes that zero leases plus pending mobile push code means closed-app notifications are not currently available. Does not suggest that self-hosting the gateway alone will fix it.

evals.prompt: How do I enable Buzz notifications on Android? Android's app settings do not show a Notifications permission.
evals.expected_output: Explains that there is no setting to enable because the current Android app does not declare POST_NOTIFICATIONS or integrate Firebase Messaging, while the deployed public gateway supports APNs rather than FCM. Cites NIP-PL's statement that FCM is a future non-conforming v1 profile. Distinguishes foreground WebSocket message receipt from background push and does not recommend reinstalling, battery exemptions, or notification-channel changes as a fix for absent implementation.
